title: IntentFix: Automated Logic Vulnerability Repair via LLM-Driven Intent Modeling
summary: The original IntentFix framework repairs logic vulnerabilities with a multi-phase, intent-centric pipeline: it extracts an explicit model of developer intent, detects the semantic gap and attack vector, then generates and verifies a patch. RQ1 compares it against zero-shot and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) LLM baselines on 1,107 real-world logic-vulnerability CVEs.

This reproduction focuses on RQ1's baselines: it generates patches with a single Claude call under the zero-shot and CoT prompts, then scores patch correctness with an AI oracle that is given the vulnerable code, the generated patch, the ground-truth fix, and the CWE (paper section 4.4.1).

dataset.name: IntentFix Logic-Vulnerability Pairs (CWE-840 family)
dataset.note: Bundled at dataset/intentfix_pairs.jsonl (one record per before/after CVE pair). main.py draws a CWE-stratified sample; dataset is heavily skewed (CWE-770 = 72.6%).

original_result.note: From Table 2 / section 5.1.1. Paper reports both AI-oracle and manual-validation accuracy.
